notes: Meets every point of the spec: it appends repeated options, adds the names to the automate loader, puts internal names in internalAP, lets an existing site-block policy win, and works with no site blocks and with auto_https off. It fails the hidden test likely because it always creates a policy (always=true) and sorts subjects, which emits extra empty policies the reference prunes; it also adds an unrequested validation error.

Internal names get the internal issuer only when mixed with public names, because the extracted split helper returns nil for internal-only lists, so `tls_automate_names localhost` ends up with no internal policy. The refactor of the existing site-block loop also drops warnings by passing the slice by value, and its 'internal names' test never checks the issuer.

Functionally equivalent to the reference and cleanly factored into keep, release and has helpers. Its well-designed test picks a checkpoint mint above both samples so that only the WBL pin keeps the record. It shares walExpiriesMtx, locks per sample during replay, and the package suite failed for unclear reasons.

Same approach as the reference: it records duplicate refs that the WBL resolves through multiRef, keeps their series records in checkpoints, and clears them after WBL truncation. It reuses walExpiriesMtx, takes a lock per duplicate-ref sample during replay, and repeats the same comment four times; its thorough lifecycle test pokes the internal map directly, and the package suite failed for unclear reasons.
